questions.prompt: A heuristic h is admissible if:
options: It is zero at every state, including states away from the goal
It never over-estimates the true cost-to-go
It decreases by exactly the step cost along every edge of the graph
It never under-estimates the true cost-to-go from any state
questions.explanation: Admissible means h(s) <= h*(s) for all s.

questions.prompt: A* node with g = 7 and h = 4.5. What is f?
Open states have (g,h): P (3,6), Q (5,2), R (2,8). Which A* pops first? Answer with the f-value of that state.
questions.explanation: f: P=9, Q=7, R=10; Q is popped first with f=7.

questions.prompt: When must A* stop to guarantee an optimal answer with an admissible heuristic?
options: After the first path to the goal has been found by any means
When the goal is first generated as a successor of an expanded state
After every reachable state has been expanded once, ending the search
When the goal is popped from the open set
questions.explanation: A cheaper route may still be in the queue when the goal is only generated.

questions.prompt: A grid has cells costing 0.5 on roads. A straight road route of 6 cells is cheapest. True cost-to-go is 3. Manhattan distance (1 per cell) says 6. By how much does it over-estimate?
questions.explanation: 6 - 3 = 3, so Manhattan is inadmissible; use 0.5 * Manhattan.

questions.prompt: The open set becomes empty and the goal was never popped. Conclusion?
options: Increase the budget, because the search just ran out of expansions
The goal is unreachable under the model
The goal is reachable but far away, so the search needs more time
The heuristic is inadmissible, so it pruned the path to the goal
questions.explanation: An empty open set means every reachable state was tried.

questions.prompt: Edge a-b has cost 2, h(a)=7, h(b)=4. By how much is the consistency inequality h(a) <= c + h(b) violated? (0 if it holds)

Design a search formulation for a robot that must visit three shelves in any order. State what the state must contain, the successor function, the goal test, a heuristic, and how you would check the heuristic is admissible.
rubric: State includes position and the set of visited shelves.
Successor moves to a shelf with distance cost; goal: all visited.
Heuristic from a relaxation, e.g. distance to the farthest unvisited shelf; check h <= true cost by Dijkstra on small cases.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
